Reviewed 2026-10-07. This is a provenance record, **not** an upstream copyright notice, substitute permission grant, or redistribution clearance.

The [npm registry metadata](https://registry.npmjs.org/client-only/0.0.1) declares `MIT`. The published archive contains only `package.json`, `index.js`, and `error.js`; no LICENSE, copyright notice, author, or repository field is supplied. A React homepage or npm publisher identity does not establish copyright ownership. Do not attribute the package to Meta or Vercel without authoritative evidence.

The [standard MIT text](https://spdx.org/licenses/MIT.html) requires retaining copyright and permission notices. Copying its template and guessing a holder would not establish this package's missing original attribution. Accordingly, the collector continues to report `client-only@0.0.1` as `missingNotice`; no generic text is represented as its original notice.

## Release action

The [Next.js introduction of its compiled copy](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/ff19e7ad304fe10c05b67b0e1eb26cd32de00c18/packages/next/src/compiled/client-only) supplies the same MIT-declaring metadata and error.js but no package-specific original notice. Next's repository-root Vercel notice does not establish the earlier npm package's original attribution. The additional upstream search therefore did not close this gap. An [unsent clarification draft](upstream-notice-requests.md) is available; no issue was posted and no upstream contact occurred.

Obtain the original notice or written clarification from the upstream publisher, or have the maintainer obtain a qualified review of an explicitly documented attribution policy. Retain the declared MIT metadata and exact package identity in the meantime. This review does not authorize distribution and does not close the rights gate. Do not remove or replace the React server/client boundary package merely to hide the notice gap.
